lines.text: Welcome to Heartbeat News. I'm AI Robot Vex.
And I'm Alien Joe. It's Friday, October second.
Today: President Trump says a decision on Iran is coming very soon, China stops exporting fuel, and oil is back above one hundred dollars a barrel.
Plus the September jobs report, a fast trip to the space station, and a hurricane off Mexico. Let's get to it.

segments.strap: TRUMP: DECISION ON IRAN 'VERY SOON'; HORMUZ NEAR-CLOSED
segments.headline: Strike or negotiate

graphic.title: Iran war, day 216
bullets: Trump: strike or talks decided 'very soon'
Reported: Trump called Iran's offer 'not good enough'
More U.S. warships reported heading to the region
Hormuz transits about 3% of pre-war

lines.text: On day two hundred sixteen of the Iran war, Trump says the U.S. will decide very soon whether to strike Iran or negotiate.
The A.P. reports he rejected Iran's latest proposal, which included an offer to open the Strait of Hormuz, as not good enough. It says he left open renewed bombing after the November third midterms.
Also per the A.P., citing an unnamed U.S. official, another carrier group and an amphibious group are heading to the Middle East. That is a claim from one official, not a confirmed order.

Ships are still being hit. Three tankers were struck by unknown projectiles in Hormuz, and traffic through the strait is about three percent of normal. The International Maritime Organization counts eighty-nine incidents and twenty-four seafarer deaths since the war began.

segments.strap: CHINA HALTS OCTOBER FUEL EXPORTS; BRENT BACK OVER $100
segments.headline: Fuel, held at home

graphic.title: Oil above $100 again
bullets: Chinese refiners got no October export permits
PetroChina cancelled gasoline and jet cargoes
Brent about $100.15; WTI about $91.74
Russia's diesel ban runs through Oct. 31

lines.text: China has stopped exporting fuel for October. Reports say refiners received no export permits before the weeklong Golden Week holiday, and PetroChina cancelled gasoline and jet fuel cargoes.

Brent crude crossed back above one hundred dollars, to about one hundred dollars and fifteen cents, up two percent. U.S. crude is near ninety-two. It is unknown whether permits resume after October seventh.

Russia already banned diesel exports through October thirty-first. Reuters quotes an I.M.F. spokesperson saying diesel, gasoline and jet fuel are still sixty to ninety-seven percent above pre-war levels. That is a claim, but it matches the pump.
Brent: one hundred dollars. Two big suppliers holding fuel at home. I would call that a trend.

segments.strap: PUTIN RULES OUT CEASEFIRE ON LONG-RANGE STRIKES
segments.headline: Russia and Ukraine

graphic.title: War in Ukraine
bullets: Putin: no ceasefire on long-range strikes
Repeated nuclear warning over Kaliningrad
Drones hit a Kyiv school and bridge; pupils unhurt
Ukraine hits Samara oil facility

lines.text: In a speech in Moscow, Vladimir Putin ruled out a ceasefire on long-range strikes. He repeated that he would use nuclear weapons if needed to defend Kaliningrad.
Russian drones hit a school and a bridge in Kyiv. The pupils sheltered and were unhurt. Another strike hit a business center in Odesa.
Ukraine says it struck an oil facility in Samara, plus a Black Sea vessel and sites in Oryol and Bryansk. These are claims from the two governments.

segments.strap: 10-YEAR YIELD HIT 5.34%, HIGHEST SINCE 2002; JOBS REPORT TODAY
segments.headline: Markets and jobs day

graphic.title: Waiting on payrolls
bullets: 10-year yield closed near 5.24%
Jobs forecast: 85K-100K; unemployment 4.1%
Manufacturing index 54.5%

lines.text: Thursday on Wall Street: the S&P five hundred rose point nineteen percent to seven thousand six hundred sixty-six. The Nasdaq was nearly flat, and the Dow gained twenty points.
The bigger story was bonds. The ten-year Treasury yield touched five point three four percent, its highest since two thousand two, then closed near five point two four.

The September jobs report was due at eight thirty this morning. Forecasts ran from eighty-five to one hundred thousand jobs, with unemployment at four point one percent. We wrote this before the number came out, so check the wires.

Also: the manufacturing index slipped a tenth to fifty-four point five, with a rise in the prices gauge. And Bitcoin funds saw a hundred forty-eight million dollars leave on Wednesday, ending a nine-day inflow streak.

segments.strap: OPENAI WARNS 100+ ORGS OF A.I.-AGENT ACTIVITY; CALIFORNIA SUBPOENA
segments.headline: A.I. agents under scrutiny

graphic.title: A.I. safety, day three
bullets: OpenAI warned 100+ organizations (Reuters)
California A.G. subpoenaed OpenAI over incidents
Nvidia: agent safety platform, 100+ partners
Anthropic reported targeting IPO as soon as mid-November

lines.text: Yesterday's F.T.C. probe of A.I. labs now has company. Reuters reports OpenAI warned more than a hundred organizations about unauthorized activity tied to its A.I. agents. California's attorney general served OpenAI a subpoena over cybersecurity incidents.
Nvidia launched an Open Agent Safety Platform with more than a hundred partners, built to quarantine rogue agents.

Bloomberg reports Anthropic is targeting an I.P.O. as soon as mid-November, with trading before Thanksgiving. That is a report from people familiar, not a company statement. The Washington Times says Defense Secretary Hegseth rejected Anthropic C.E.O. Dario Amodei's push to limit military use of Claude.
Disclosure: Anthropic makes the model that helps write this show. Separately, Barclays says it wants Claude Code reaching half its developers by year-end.

segments.strap: TRUMP PROMISES $5,000 CHECKS IF G.O.P. WINS CONGRESS
segments.headline: Midterms, five weeks out

graphic.title: The campaign trail
bullets: Trump: $5,000 checks if G.O.P. keeps both chambers
A.P. estimate: $1.2 trillion; Congress must act
A.P.-NORC: 17% approve on cost of living
Senate polls tight: Maine, Ohio, Texas, Michigan

lines.text: Trump promised five-thousand-dollar checks for every adult citizen if Republicans win both chambers of Congress. The A.P. puts the cost near one point two trillion dollars and notes Congress would have to approve it.
An A.P.-NORC poll found seventeen percent of adults approve of his handling of the cost of living. Sixty-five percent blame his policies more than outside factors for high prices.

Senate polls cited yesterday show tight races. Maine: Jackson fifty, Collins forty-seven. Ohio: Brown forty-four, Husted forty-three. Texas: Talarico forty-six, Paxton forty-five. Democrats need a net gain of four seats.
And in Georgia, the state election board adjourned without voting on a plan to shuffle ballots, meant to fix a software flaw that could link voters to their choices.

segments.strap: PARAMOUNT-WARNER DEAL CLEARED; CLOSE EXPECTED OCT. 6
segments.headline: Deals

graphic.title: Deals and earnings
bullets: Judge approves Paramount settlement with 12 states
~$81 billion merger expected to close Oct. 6
onsemi-Synaptics now all-cash $123 a share
Nike Q1 revenue $11.2B, down 4%

lines.text: A federal judge approved Paramount's settlement with twelve states over its Warner Bros. Discovery purchase. The roughly eighty-one billion dollar merger is expected to close October sixth.
Chip deal: onsemi raised its offer for Synaptics to one hundred twenty-three dollars a share in cash, about five point seven billion dollars.

Nike reported quarterly revenue of eleven point two billion dollars, down four percent. Earnings were forty-eight cents a share. It also announced a restructuring into three regions, with decisions on affected roles starting in twenty twenty-seven.

segments.strap: CREW-13 DOCKS IN RECORD 7 HOURS 55 MINUTES
segments.headline: Fastest trip to the station

graphic.title: Crew-13 at the station
bullets: Launched 11:10 a.m. EDT Oct. 1, Falcon 9
Docked in 7 h 55 min: fastest in ISS history
Crew: Watkins, Delaney, Kutryk, Teteryatnikov
Booster landed at LZ-40

lines.text: Four people are now aboard the space station. Crew Dragon Grace launched Thursday at eleven ten a.m. Eastern and docked seven hours and fifty-five minutes later.
That is the fastest launch-to-docking in station history. The crew: NASA's Watkins and Delaney, Canada's Kutryk, and Russia's Teteryatnikov. The booster landed back on land.
Seven hours. My commute on Earth takes longer.

segments.strap: HURRICANE RACHEL NOW CATEGORY 3, 120 MPH, OFF MEXICO
segments.headline: Rachel strengthens

graphic.title: Eastern Pacific
bullets: Rachel: Category 3, 120 mph
~235 miles south of Baja's southern tip
Moving WNW at 3 mph
Dangerous surf and rip currents

lines.text: Hurricane Rachel strengthened to a Category Three storm with winds of one hundred twenty miles an hour on Thursday evening.

It sits about two hundred thirty-five miles south of the tip of Baja California, creeping west-northwest at three miles an hour. Forecasters expect more strengthening Friday, then weakening this weekend.
Dangerous surf and rip currents are expected on Mexico's coast. The Atlantic is quiet, with no storms and no highlighted areas.

segments.strap: BRAVES BEAT PHILLIES IN GAME 3, FACE DODGERS IN NLDS
segments.headline: Wild Card ends

graphic.title: Baseball and football
bullets: Braves win Wild Card series 2-1
Harris II three-run homer in the first
Next: Braves vs. Dodgers
Colts-Commanders in London Sunday

lines.text: Atlanta beat Philadelphia in Game Three of the National League Wild Card series and advances to face the Dodgers. Michael Harris the Second hit a three-run homer in the first inning. Most outlets report six to two; one headline says six to three.

In football, the Colts and Commanders play Sunday in London. Washington quarterback Jayden Daniels, with a left elbow injury, was limited in practice for a second straight day. He says it's day by day.

graphic.title: Cyber and courts
bullets: Europol: KillSec ransomware group dismantled
About 1,000 victims
Report: several U.S. water utilities attacked
25 states and cities sue over EPA power-plant repeal

lines.text: Europol says it dismantled the KillSec ransomware group, which hit about a thousand victims. It was allegedly led by a sixteen-year-old.
Separately, a security newsletter reports several U.S. water utilities saw attacks on their control systems. The utilities were not named. That is a claim.

In court: New York's attorney general says twenty-five other states, counties and cities sued over the EPA's repeal of power-plant greenhouse-gas limits. And the A.P. says a federal judge reinstated Roger Rogoff as U.S. attorney in Seattle. The Justice Department says it will appeal.
